rows.steps: [{"description": "You arrive at the panel. The VFD HIM displays 'Inhibit'. The drive will not start from the keypad or the terminal block. What is your first action?", "id": 1, "options": [{"consequence": "You find that the factory STO jumper between terminals S1, S2, and S+ is missing on the new drive. The 'Inhibit' status on a PowerFlex 525 typically indicates the STO circuit is open.", "correct": true, "id": "a", "reading": "Visual inspection shows empty terminals at S1, S2, and S+.", "text": "Check the Safe Torque Off (STO) jumper or wiring on the control terminal block."}, {"consequence": "The drive resets and parameters are reloaded, but the 'Inhibit' status remains. This wastes time as 'Inhibit' is a hardware safety state, not a parameter issue.", "correct": false, "id": "b", "reading": "HIM still displays 'Inhibit'.", "text": "Attempt to reset the drive to factory defaults and reload the parameters."}, {"consequence": "You measure 480VAC across all three phases. The power is fine, but the drive still won't start. 'Inhibit' is a control/safety issue, not a main power issue.", "correct": false, "id": "c", "reading": "L1-L2: 480V, L2-L3: 480V, L1-L3: 480V.", "text": "Measure the incoming 3-phase line voltage to ensure all phases are present."}], "title": "Initial Assessment of 'Inhibit' Status"}, {"description": "You realize the STO (Safe Torque Off) circuit is open. The original drive had a safety relay wired to it, but the new drive was installed without transferring those wires or installing the factory jumper. What do you do next?", "id": 2, "options": [{"consequence": "The drive starts, but you have bypassed a critical machine safety circuit, violating safety protocols and putting operators at risk.", "correct": false, "id": "a", "reading": "Drive runs, but safety is compromised.", "text": "Install a standard wire jumper between S1, S2, and S+ to bypass the safety circuit and get the machine running immediately."}, {"consequence": "The schematics show that the safety relay outputs should be wired to S1 and S2, with S+ providing the 24VDC source. You identify the loose wires in the wireway.", "correct": true, "id": "b", "reading": "Schematics confirm STO wiring requirements.", "text": "Check the electrical schematics to determine how the STO circuit was originally wired to the safety relay."}, {"consequence": "You cannot disable the hardware STO circuit via parameters on a PowerFlex 525. The drive remains in 'Inhibit' state.", "correct": false, "id": "c", "reading": "Parameter change rejected or ineffective.", "text": "Change parameter t105 [Safety Open En] to disable the safety circuit in software."}], "title": "Addressing the STO Circuit"}, {"description": "You have located the safety relay wires that were left disconnected during the drive swap. How do you proceed to safely restore operation?", "id": 3, "options": [{"consequence": "The drive still shows 'Inhibit' because the dedicated STO terminals (S1, S2) are still open. The safety circuit will not function correctly.", "correct": false, "id": "a", "reading": "HIM displays 'Inhibit'.", "text": "Connect the safety relay wires to the digital inputs (Terminals 5 and 6) instead of the STO terminals."}, {"consequence": "The 'Inhibit' status clears when the safety relay is reset. You test the E-stop, verifying the drive drops out safely. The machine is now safe and operational.", "correct": true, "id": "b", "reading": "HIM displays 'Stopped', ready to run.", "text": "Wire the safety relay contacts to the STO terminals (S1, S2, and S+) according to the schematic, then test the safety circuit."}, {"consequence": "The drive runs, but failing to test a safety circuit after modifying it is a major safety violation. You cannot guarantee the E-stop works.", "correct": false, "id": "c", "reading": "Drive runs, safety unverified.", "text": "Wire the safety relay to the STO terminals, but do not test the safety circuit to save time since it's a new drive."}], "title": "Finalizing the Installation"}]
rows.equipment: ["Allen-Bradley PowerFlex 525 VFD", "Digital Multimeter", "Electrical Schematics", "3-Phase AC Motor"]
rows.toolReadings: {"flashlight": {"description": "Reveals that terminals S1, S2, and S+ on the new VFD have no wires or jumpers installed.", "label": "Terminal Block Inspection"}, "multimeter": {"label": "Control Voltage at Safety Relay", "unit": "VDC", "value": "24.1"}, "prints": {"description": "Shows dual-channel safety relay outputs wired to VFD terminals S1 and S2, sourced from S+.", "label": "STO Wiring Diagram"}}
